subject: Next Steps: Model selection evidence and TPS/latency deep-links
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@signalmed.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-15T15:04:00-08:00
Subject: Next Steps: Model selection evidence and TPS/latency deep-links

Thanks again for a productive demo today — appreciate the clarity on the two primary inference paths (real-time summary service vs. batch document enrichment). Quick recap and suggested next steps: 

- Recommendation (shortlist): RWI-7B-quant (8-bit) and RWX-13B-ptq. We picked these to cover low-latency interactive flows and higher-quality batch runs respectively.
- Performance evidence: I've attached a concise Redwood performance slate (redwood-perf-slate-20260115.csv) with TPS and latency percentiles across sequence-length buckets we discussed. 
- Prompt sets: Attached a first-pass prompt pack tailored to your summary/enrichment prompts (signalmed-prompt-sets-v1.txt). Please iterate with your SMEs if any phrasing needs adjusting.

As a next step, could you confirm which workflow you want us to prioritize for a short verification run (interactive summarization or nightly enrichment)? Once you confirm, we will: 
1) Spin a 48-hour dedicated verification window with pinned model versions.
2) Share a small dashboard with p50/p95/p99 latency and observed token throughput (TPS) broken down by seq-length buckets (128/512/2048).
3) Include a regression watchlist: we will baseline quality on your 200-case prompt set and flag drift compared to the demo snapshot.

Attachments: redwood-perf-slate-20260115.csv (CSV, 1.1MB), signalmed-prompt-sets-v1.txt (TXT, 14KB).

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick sync if helpful.

Best,
Grace
Grace O'Connor
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Martinez <alex@signalmed.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordana Lim <jordana.lim@signalmed.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-16T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Next Steps: Model selection evidence and TPS/latency deep-links

Thanks Grace — helpful summary. Quick clarifying Qs from our infra and ML lead so we can scope the verification run: 

1) For the interactive summarization path, can you call out p99 latency at 512 and 2048 token windows for RWI-7B-quant? We care about 95th-99th tail for user-facing latency SLAs.
2) For RWX-13B-ptq, what's the observed TPS when batching with 4 concurrent requests at avg seq=512?
3) On data residency: we'll want logs retained for 30 days and stubbed audit traces for the demo. Any blockers on the private-control-plane option for a short window?

Also, one ask on quality: we'll run the 200-case prompt set and expect Redwood to surface the top 20 regression candidates (examples that changed significantly vs the baseline). Can you confirm that will be included in the verification dashboard?

If we can get those numbers laid out and a tentative 48-hour window next week, we can align internal stakeholders.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Martinez
Head of ML Ops
SignalMed

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@signalmed.ai>, Jordana Lim <jordana.lim@signalmed.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-17T11:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Next Steps: Model selection evidence and TPS/latency deep-links

Alex — answering each bullet with the Redwood-verified slate details and what we will surface in the verification window:

1) RWI-7B-quant (interactive) — latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) at two seq buckets (numbers are from our Redwood verification runs using your demo prompt patterns):
   - seq=512: p50 35ms, p95 78ms, p99 120ms
   - seq=2048: p50 150ms, p95 310ms, p99 460ms
   Notes: p99 increases due to KV-cache and attention probed for long contexts; we can mitigate with shorter sliding windows or prefix caching for your UI workflow.

2) RWX-13B-ptq (batch, quantized) — observed throughput when batching=4 and avg seq=512:
   - Effective TPS (tokens/sec across GPU pool): ~1,350 TPS
   - Per-request latency (end-to-end) median ~420ms, p95 ~920ms (higher variability due to memory compaction on longer context).

3) Data residency / logs: For the 48-hour verification window we can enable private-control-plane audit stubs and retain structured traces for 30 days (searchable logs + hashed request ids). No blockers — we'll provision a short-lived VPC peering with audit-only export.

Quality/regression: yes — during the verification window we'll run your 200-case prompt pack and produce a regression watchlist of the top 20 changed outputs compared to the demo baseline. The verification dashboard will include diffs, similarity scores, and links to the raw traces so your ML team can triage quickly.

Operational notes / recommended config for the window:
- Models pinned: RWI-7B-quant:v1.3, RWX-13B-ptq:v2.0
- Autoscale: disabled (fixed pool) to get stable TPS numbers
- Batching policy: dynamic batching with max_batch=8 and latency target 200ms for interactive path
- Caching: prefix KV caching enabled for seq>256 patterns

I've uploaded the full Redwood-verified performance profile (CSV) to the shared Drive link and included a short summary here. If you'd like, we can also provide GPU-level traces for a single sample request to show kernel timings.

Proposed next steps: 
- We can run the 48-hour verification window starting Monday 2026-01-19 09:00 PT if that works for your team.
- I'll schedule a brief handoff call (15 min) to confirm prompt versions and success criteria.

If that timing works, let me know and we'll send the invite and provision the environment.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Lead Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Attachment references: redwood-perf-slate-20260115.csv (contains broken-out TPS & latency p50/p95/p99 by seq bucket).
